That is NOT what the gate compares against: scripts/lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head('f9b4dea..7d089a8') returns f9b4dea... MUTATION PROBES -- I deliberately broke what this PR asserts and what it relies on, and checked whether anything failed. Working tree verified clean (git status --porcelain empty) after every probe.

PROBE 1 (the decisive one). The document's closing section, "The rule this establishes", asserts: "If a record produced that way is filed at all, that field must read `true`, which means it will not satisfy the gate -- which is the correct outcome." I filed a schema-complete record at reviews/32/probe.json with reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author set to true, reviewed_commit set to the reviewable head, verdict AGREE. Result: "NOTICE: ... reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author=true -- this review is NOT independent by construction ...", then "lwb-lanes check passed", EXIT=0. The identical record with the field set to false: "lwb-lanes check passed", EXIT=0. The two are indistinguishable in exit status; only a NOTICE line differs, and scripts/lwb_lanes.main() prints notices and then returns 0 regardless. See FINDING 1.

PROBE 2. Same record, reviewed_commit set to the PR head 7d089a8 instead of the reviewable head: correctly rejected as STALE, EXIT=1. The freshness check is not vacuous in that direction.

PROBE 3 (content binding). I replaced the ENTIRE contents of reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md with a single line of deliberate nonsense asserting the opposite of the document, committed it, and re-ran the gate with the same review record in place. Result: "lwb-lanes check passed", EXIT=0, and resolve_reviewable_head still returned f9b4dea. A review record for this PR is not bound to one byte of what the PR actually says. See FINDING 2.

PROBE 4 (is the new file actually guarded?). reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md IS in scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py's scan set (confirmed present in `git ls-files "*.md"`, 37 files). I appended two volatile state claims to it ("main is currently at commit 9b374b5...", "there are 3 open PRs"): the check FAILED, EXIT=1, naming both claims at reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md:72. That gate is genuinely non-vacuous on the file this PR adds, and the document's existing use of specific historical shas does not trip it. No finding here -- recording it because a passing gate that had never looked at the new file would have been worth knowing about.

FINDINGS -- three.

FINDING 1 (BLOCKING, and the reason for DISAGREE). The document states a falsehood about this repository's own gate, in the one paragraph whose job is to state the rule it establishes. "that field must read `true`, which means it will not satisfy the gate" is false, measured in PROBE 1: a record declaring true PASSES lwb-lanes with EXIT=0 and a printed NOTICE. This is not a subtle discrepancy and it is not my inference from reading code. Three independent sources in this repository already say the opposite: (a) scripts/lwb_lanes._review_ok returns the reviewer_id after the `if dispatched and notices is not None:` branch rather than returning None, so the record still counts; (b) that function's own comment says "it is recorded and surfaced, never trusted as proof"; (c) reviews/schema.json's description for the field says, verbatim, "`true` does not fail the gate (the gate cannot tell a genuinely independent reviewer from one that simply declares itself independent), but scripts/lwb_lanes.py prints a NOTICE for it". The PR contradicts a description sitting in the reviews/ directory it is filing into.

Why this is material rather than a nit. The document's stated purpose is precision about provenance, and its practical consequence for a reader is the claim that honest reporting would have been mechanically blocking. It would not have been. Had #27's reviewer written `true`, lwb-lanes would still have gone green and #27 would still have merged -- with a NOTICE in the log that nothing fails on. A future reader who believes this paragraph will believe a safeguard exists that does not.

The claim is also in direct tension with the paragraph immediately above it in the same section, which correctly says "Nothing in scripts/lwb_lanes.py can distinguish a cron-dispatched run from a manually-fired one". I considered the charitable reading -- that "the gate" means D27's independence requirement rather than the lwb-lanes check -- and I do not think it survives: the surrounding sentences name scripts/lwb_lanes.py explicitly, "which is the correct outcome" implies a blocking result, and in a document written to be exact about this gate, "the gate" cannot be loose. Either way the sentence needs to change. The fix is small: say that a `true` record still satisfies lwb-lanes and only raises a NOTICE, and that the enforcement of this rule is therefore procedural too -- which is the same honest shape the rest of the document already uses for the dispatch limitation.

FINDING 2 (STRUCTURAL; NOT charged to this PR's author -- scripts/lwb_lanes.py is untouched by this diff). For a pull request whose commits touch ONLY reviews/ (and/or proof/), the shared-path review gate is vacuous with respect to that PR's content. classify_path calls reviews/ shared, so the gate DEMANDS an independent review; resolve_reviewable_head excludes record-only commits, so the head the record must attest to is the BASE commit -- here f9b4dea, an already-merged main that this PR does not modify. PROBE 3 demonstrates the consequence empirically: gutting the document entirely leaves the gate green. The skip rule is correct and load-bearing for ordinary PRs (it stops a review record invalidating itself), but in the degenerate all-records PR it defines the reviewed content out of existence. Note the same will hold for the proof/32.json commit FINDING 3 requires: that is also record-only, so it will not move the reviewable head either. I am recording this rather than proposing a patch, because fixing it means changing a shared script and that is not this PR's job -- but a reader should not take a green lwb-lanes on a reviews/-only PR as evidence that anything in it was reviewed. That includes this record.

FINDING 3 (BLOCKING for merge; already red in CI; outside my write scope). PR #32 carries no proof/*.json record for itself. scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 32 exits 1: "PR #32 carries no proof/*.json record for itself." This fails the lwb-proof-pr step on all six matrix legs right now. My review record cannot fix it -- I am authorized to write only reviews/32/ -- so it needs a proof/32.json from the author. I mention it because a reader seeing a review record land might otherwise expect the PR to go green; it will not.

ONE THING THE CORRECTION UNDER-REPORTS (minor, not blocking). The document locates the defect in the JSON boolean, and says "The defect is in the provenance claim, not the review." But the #27 record's notes field ALSO asserts it in prose, as its opening sentence: "Independent cloud reviewer, dispatched by a schedule (the clock), not by the author's session." That sentence is wrong on the same facts and is not mentioned. Since the document's argument for leaving the record unamended is that the record should keep saying what the reviewer wrote, naming both places would strengthen it, not weaken it. I would not block on this alone.

MY OWN NEAR-MISSES, recorded because hiding them would make this record worth less:
1. I nearly cleared FINDING 1 falsely. My first run of PROBE 1 used a record missing the required commit_author_agent field, so all three variants -- head-sha, false and true -- failed identically with a schema error. Read carelessly that output says "true is rejected", which would have let the document's claim stand. The three FAILs being byte-identical across three supposedly different inputs is what made me re-run with a schema-complete record, and the real result was the opposite. A probe that fails for the wrong reason looks exactly like a probe that proves your point.
2. I nearly charged FINDING 2 to this author. The vacuity is in scripts/lwb_lanes.py, which this diff does not touch at all; this PR only happens to be the shape that exposes it. Charging a pre-existing structural property to the PR in front of me would have been the "innocent PR" error, and I caught it by diffing before writing rather than after.
3. I fetched origin/main before running lwb_check_state_claims.py specifically because a stale origin/main is documented to make it accuse a correct document. It passed. Had I not fetched, I do not know whether I would have reported a false positive against HANDOFF.md.

VERDICT. DISAGREE, on FINDING 1 alone. Everything else in this document is accurate, carefully reasoned, and worth landing: the central correction is true, corroborated from inside the repository by a matching session token and from GitHub by a timeline that does not fit the cron account, and the decision not to rewrite a landed record is right. I am not blocking on the correction. I am blocking because a document written to fix a false provenance claim closes by making a false claim about the mechanism that would have caught it, and because that claim is contradicted by reviews/schema.json sitting in the same directory the file is filed into. The fix is a sentence or two, and the PR already needs another push for FINDING 3 regardless, so this costs the author nothing extra. Correct the paragraph and I would expect the next reviewer to AGREE.
